instru_desc: Questionnaires, survey modules, validated scales and coding schemes used to measure public opinion and attitudes toward refugees and related constructs.
instru_narr: Include full questionnaires or modules that contain refugee-attitude items, validated scales for measuring xenophobia/social distance, vignette instruments about refugee scenarios, interviewer guidelines and codebooks, and instruments for measuring contact or media exposure relevant to refugee attitudes. Exclude instruments focused exclusively on administrative registration of refugees, technical asylum procedures, or instruments measuring migration policy capacity without attitudinal components.

instru_desc: Survey instruments and psychometric tools used to measure global life satisfaction and subjective well‑being (questionnaire modules, SWLS, translation/validation documents, scoring manuals).
instru_narr: Include validated instruments (Satisfaction With Life Scale, single‑item global measures used in ESS/WVS), questionnaire modules containing life satisfaction items, translation and cultural adaptation reports, and documentation on administration and scoring. Exclude instruments that only measure domain‑specific satisfaction or affect without a global life satisfaction component.

instru_desc: Validated instruments and administration materials for measuring general self‑efficacy (e.g., General Self‑Efficacy Scale by Schwarzer & Jerusalem), translations, scoring guidelines and psychometric evaluations.
instru_narr: Include scale instruments (full item lists), scoring manuals, normative data, translation/adaptation reports, and guidance for use in surveys or interventions. Exclude instruments that exclusively measure domain‑specific self‑efficacy (e.g., academic self‑efficacy) when no general self‑efficacy instrument is present.

instru_desc: Survey scales, questionnaires, codebooks and coding schemes used to measure antisemitism and to record antisemitic incidents (measurement instruments, vignette protocols, incident classification schemas).
instru_narr: Include validated antisemitism scales, questionnaire modules used in national/international surveys, coding manuals for incident databases, and methodological documentation on administering sensitive items. Exclude generic prejudice instruments that do not include antisemitism items and technical police systems unrelated to research classification.

instru_desc: Survey modules, questionnaires, coding schemes and analytic tools for measuring employment and work (labour force modules, occupational/industry coding manuals, job quality indices).
instru_narr: Include standard labour force questionnaires, interviewer instructions, occupational/industry coding manuals (ISCO, NACE), job classification concordances, job quality measurement tools, and documentation for administrative employment registers. Exclude instruments that measure only non‑work constructs or that are irrelevant to measuring employment (e.g., medical assessment tools without occupational linkage).

instru_desc: Validated questionnaires and measurement tools for assessing occupational workload and psychosocial/physical burdens at work (e.g. JCQ, COPSOQ, ERI, burnout inventories).
instru_narr: Include descriptions and use of validated instruments for measuring job demands and occupational stress such as the Job Content Questionnaire (JCQ), Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaire (COPSOQ), Effort-Reward Imbalance (ERI) questionnaire, Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI), Perceived Stress Scale (when used in occupational context), and workplace exposure assessment protocols. Also include time-use diaries, ergonomic assessment checklists, and employer absence records used to quantify burden. Exclude management tools or organizational audits that do not produce measures of workload or psychosocial/physical burden.

instru_desc: Standardized instruments and scales to measure job satisfaction and related constructs (e.g. JSS, MSQ, single-item measures, engagement scales).
instru_narr: Include established instruments such as the Job Satisfaction Survey (JSS), Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire (MSQ), single-item global satisfaction questions, and related engagement or commitment instruments (e.g. Utrecht Work Engagement Scale where relevant). Include survey modules and questionnaires used in labour and working conditions surveys to assess satisfaction. Exclude instruments that measure only managerial performance or customer satisfaction without employee-reported satisfaction.

instru_desc: Instruments for assessing workplace organization and company-level practices such as employer questionnaires, organizational audits, and workplace assessment protocols.
instru_narr: Include employer survey instruments, organizational climate audits, management practice indexes, workplace risk assessment tools, and standardized establishment survey modules used to measure company-level working conditions and HR practices. Include protocols for matched employer-employee data collection. Exclude business tools focused solely on market performance or customer analytics that do not assess employee work or workplace organization.

instru_desc: Measurement tools for assessing work–life balance and related constructs such as work–family conflict scales, time-use diaries, and flexible work use modules.
instru_narr: Include validated scales like the Work–Family Conflict Scale (Netemeyer et al.), Work–Life Balance questionnaires, time-use diary methodologies, survey modules on telework and flexible scheduling (e.g. EWCS modules), and instruments measuring caregiving burden. Include employer policies inventories that record leave entitlements and flexible arrangements. Exclude general well‑being instruments that do not include work–life items or tools measuring only organizational performance.

instru_desc: Standard instruments and classification systems used in work and employment research such as labour force questionnaires, ISCO occupational coding, industry classifications, and working conditions survey modules.
instru_narr: Include tools used to measure employment and work characteristics: labour force survey questionnaires, time-use diaries for work, occupational and industry classification systems (ISCO, NACE/WZ), standardized working conditions and occupational health survey modules (e.g. EWCS items), and administrative record linkage protocols. Include validated scales for job quality and work-related health. Exclude instruments unrelated to measuring work or employment.

instru_desc: Questionnaires, coding schemes and measurement instruments used to assess changes in work, occupations and job tasks.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments: survey modules and questionnaires on job tasks and task routineness, measures of digitalisation and platform work, occupational history calendars, instruments for coding occupations (ISCO concordances, national mappings), workplace change assessment tools, employer survey modules on restructuring and technology adoption, and validated scales for measuring skill use and task content. Exclude: technical engineering tools unrelated to labor outcomes, clinical assessment instruments not designed for workplace research.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools used to measure and classify occupations, career histories and vocational competences.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments: occupational classification manuals (ISCO, national classifications), job history calendars, questionnaires on vocational training and career development, coding tools and concordances between classification systems, career trajectory mapping tools, and competency assessment instruments. Exclude: measurement tools unrelated to occupational analysis (e.g. clinical psychometrics not adapted to workplace contexts).

instru_desc: Validated questionnaires and measurement tools for assessing job satisfaction and related workplace well‑being constructs.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments: standard job satisfaction measures (Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire, Job Satisfaction Survey, single-item measures used in large surveys), scales assessing facets of job satisfaction, psychosocial workplace instruments (e.g. COPSOQ, Job Content Questionnaire, Effort–Reward Imbalance), and survey modules capturing satisfaction-related constructs. Include translations and psychometric documentation. Exclude: instruments not targeted at job-related satisfaction or those without psychometric validation.

instru_desc: Assessment instruments and tools for measuring working conditions, occupational hazards, health and psychosocial work environment.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments: COPSOQ, Job Content Questionnaire (demand-control-support), Effort–Reward Imbalance scale, EWCS survey modules, workplace risk assessment checklists, ergonomic assessment tools, shift-work questionnaires, safety reporting systems, and structured observational tools. Include translations, validation studies and guidance for application. Exclude: clinical diagnostic instruments unrelated to workplace exposures or tools solely for industrial engineering design without occupational-health focus.

instru_desc: Instruments, register systems and survey modules used to measure unemployment, job-search behaviour and programme participation.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments: labour force survey questionnaires (unemployment modules), administrative unemployment registers, benefit payment and caseworker databases, job-search and unemployment spell calendars, standardized coding for labour-status categories, and evaluation tools for active labour-market programmes. Exclude: tools not designed to capture unemployment or those focused exclusively on underemployment without unemployment measures.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments used for commute assessment: travel diaries, GPS/accelerometer trackers, map-based route collection tools, commute modules in surveys, and validated scales for commuting stress.
instru_narr: Include survey modules and questionnaires asking about usual mode, travel time and distance to work; travel diaries and day reconstruction methods specifying work-trip entries; GPS tracking and smartphone apps that record routes and times; transport modelling tools for commute distance/time estimation; and psychometric scales specifically assessing commuting stress or satisfaction. Exclude instruments that record mobility only at an aggregate level without trip purpose or those unrelated to travel-to-work measurement.

instru_desc: Tools for measuring working time: time-use diaries, payroll and electronic time-stamp systems, employer scheduling software extracts, and standardized survey modules on working hours.
instru_narr: Include validated instruments and administrative sources used to measure hours and schedules: diary-based time-use instruments (with paid-work episodes), employer payroll registers and clock-in/clock-out logs, roster/schedule exports, and standard survey items from sources like the European Working Conditions Survey or Working Time Survey. Exclude general employment questionnaires lacking detailed time or schedule items.

instru_desc: Instruments to measure migration status and integration: migration questionnaires/modules, administrative registers, language proficiency tests, and acculturation/integration scales.
instru_narr: Include standard survey modules asking about birthplace, citizenship, year of immigration, reason for migration, and residence status; administrative data linkages with registries; validated instruments for language assessment; and scales measuring integration, discrimination or acculturation. Exclude instruments that do not collect clear migration identifiers or that only offer informal proxies for foreign status.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments for work-related burden: Job Content Questionnaire, Effort–Reward Imbalance instrument, Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaire, Maslach Burnout Inventory, ergonomic assessment tools and workplace exposure checklists.
instru_narr: Include validated psychometric instruments for psychosocial work factors (JCQ, ERI, COPSOQ), burnout measures (MBI), standardized ergonomic observation tools, workplace exposure assessment protocols, and administrative tools for recording occupational incidents and sick leave. Exclude generic stress scales not tied to workplace conditions or ad hoc measures lacking validation for occupational research.

instru_desc: Tools for assessing the work–burden relationship: combined survey modules (work conditions + health), validated psychosocial instruments (JCQ, COPSOQ, ERI), burnout inventories, and HR analytics linking workload and absence.
instru_narr: Include instruments and protocols designed to measure both sides of the equation: standard workplace psychosocial questionnaires combined with health and absence records, ergonomics and exposure assessment tools alongside symptom checklists, and employer data extraction methods that align work metrics with individual health/performance. Exclude tools that measure only job attributes or only health outcomes without integration capability.

instru_desc: Validated questionnaires, observational checklists and measurement tools for assessing workplace burdens and exposures.
instru_narr: Include instruments such as the Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaire (COPSOQ), Job Content Questionnaire (JCQ), Effort-Reward Imbalance (ERI) questionnaire, Maslach Burnout Inventory when used for work stress, ergonomic assessment tools (RULA, REBA), noise dosimeters, exposure measurement protocols and workplace observation checklists. Exclude tools that measure general life stress without workplace items.

instru_desc: Classification manuals, coding tools and survey modules used to record and categorize occupations.
instru_narr: Include ISCO and other occupational classification manuals, coding schemes (e.g., ISCO-08), occupation coding software and crosswalks, survey question wordings for occupation and employment, and guidance materials for coding free-text job titles. Exclude instruments unrelated to occupational coding or that measure other constructs only tangentially.

instru_desc: Coding schemes, questionnaires and tools that link education information to occupational classification and skill measurement.
instru_narr: Include ISCED and national qualification classification manuals, tools mapping qualifications to occupations, survey modules on educational history and vocational training, measures of skill mismatch, and instruments for assessing returns to education. Exclude classroom-level teaching instruments not relevant to labor market placement.

instru_desc: Validated scales and survey items for assessing job satisfaction and its facets.
instru_narr: Include instruments such as the Job Satisfaction Survey (JSS), Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire (MSQ), single-item global job satisfaction questions used in large surveys, facet scales for pay/supervision/tasks, and guidance on scoring and interpretation. Exclude clinical diagnostic tools that do not specifically measure job-related satisfaction.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools for measuring job tasks, time use and employment histories.
instru_narr: Include time-use diaries, work diary instruments, task inventories and taxonomies (e.g., O*NET mappings), employment history modules, job exposure matrices (JEMs) and survey question modules for recording employment activity. Exclude clinical functional assessments that do not specify workplace activities.

instru_desc: Survey modules, life-history calendars, coding schemes and analytical tools for measuring and analysing occupational mobility (job history questionnaires, occupational coding manuals, mobility matrices and sequence-analysis software).
instru_narr: Relevant instruments include standardized job-history modules and life-course calendars that capture start/end dates and job characteristics, occupational coding schemes (ISCO, national classifications), indices of status/skill (ISEI, prestige scales), mobility matrices and statistical/sequence-analysis tools (e.g., TraMineR) and questionnaire items eliciting reasons for job change. Exclude instruments that focus solely on employer-level measures, organizational HR systems without individual career detail, or tools unrelated to tracking job transitions.

instru_desc: Validated scales and survey items used to measure occupational attitudes and work values, such as work values inventories, job satisfaction questionnaires and modules on occupational preferences and vocational orientations.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments include standardized work-values inventories, Job Satisfaction scales (single-item or multi-item), measures of intrinsic/extrinsic motivation, career aspiration modules, and questionnaire batteries used in major social surveys to elicit work attitudes. Include translation/adaptations for German contexts. Exclude psychometric instruments unrelated to occupational attitudes (e.g., personality tests without a work-specific component) or instruments that only capture employers' perspectives.

instru_desc: Psychometric scales and survey modules for assessing professional identity and occupational self-concept, such as occupational self-efficacy scales, career identity questionnaires, and life-history tools capturing identity development.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments include validated occupational self-efficacy scales, professional identity scales/adaptations for specific professions, career adaptability and identity questionnaires (e.g., Career Adapt-Abilities items), and interview guides/life-history calendars focusing on identity formation in work. Exclude instruments measuring general personality traits or organizational-level identity measures without an individual occupational-self focus.

instru_desc: Survey modules, question batteries and experimental designs used to measure public evaluation of social policy, including vignettes, policy-specific items and comparative opinion modules.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments include standardized opinion-question batteries on welfare attitudes, modules used in comparative surveys (e.g., items on welfare support), vignette experiments assessing reactions to policy scenarios, and validated scales measuring trust in social institutions and perceived policy effectiveness. Exclude instruments focused only on administrative policy metrics or technical costing tools without measures of public evaluation.

instru_desc: Questionnaires, validated scales and measurement modules for assessing supervisor–employee relations, notably Leader–Member Exchange instruments, supervisory support scales and workplace conflict/mentoring measures.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments include the LMX-7 (or other LMX measures), perceived supervisor support scales, mentoring relationship inventories, instruments measuring supervisory fairness and abusive supervision, and multi-source feedback tools capturing dyadic relations. Exclude leadership instruments that only measure leader traits or organizational-level leadership climate without items on the dyadic supervisor–subordinate relationship.

instru_desc: Survey modules, questionnaires, standardized assessments and evaluation tools used to measure adult education and lifelong learning (e.g., AES questionnaire modules, PIAAC instruments, program evaluation templates).
instru_narr: Include validated survey instruments and questionnaire modules that capture participation in adult learning, motivations and barriers, and adult skill assessments (literacy, numeracy) such as AES and PIAAC instruments, course attendance logs, program evaluation protocols, and adult learning scales. Exclude instruments designed for primary/secondary education settings only, or clinical tools not adapted for measuring adult learning engagement.

instru_desc: Survey modules, scales and measurement tools for assessing care work, caregiver burden, time-use instruments, and occupational classification tools relevant to care sectors.
instru_narr: Include validated instruments such as caregiver burden scales (e.g., Zarit Burden Interview), time-use diary instruments, occupational classification codes for care professions (ISCO/standard national codes), caregiver questionnaires embedded in household surveys, and program evaluation tools for care services. Exclude clinical assessment tools focused only on patient diagnosis without caregiver-oriented items, or generic workplace instruments lacking care-specific items.

instru_desc: Survey instruments, validated scales and segmentation tools used to measure climate change attitudes, concern, risk perception and behavioral intent (e.g., standardized survey items, 'Six Americas' segmentation, experimental vignette protocols).
instru_narr: Include commonly used survey question batteries about climate beliefs and concern, validated psychometric scales for environmental concern (when applied to climate), segmentation instruments (e.g., Yale/George Mason 'Six Americas'), and experimental stimuli or messaging protocols used to test attitude change. Exclude instruments focused solely on technical climate literacy tests unrelated to attitudinal measures.

instru_desc: Models, measurement instruments, survey modules, remote sensing products, and tools used in climate research and policy analysis (climate models, downscaling tools, emission accounting methods, remote sensing datasets, public opinion survey modules).
instru_narr: Include climate model ensembles (CMIP), downscaling tools, remote sensing products (MODIS, GRACE), greenhouse gas accounting methodologies, climate impact assessment frameworks, vulnerability and risk assessment tools, and social-science instruments measuring climate perceptions and policy preferences. Exclude tools that do not pertain to climate-related measurement, modeling, or assessment.

instru_desc: Survey question batteries, vignettes, scales and experimental instruments designed to measure public conceptions of democracy, democratic values, legitimacy, and related constructs.
instru_narr: Include validated survey modules from major studies (e.g., World Values Survey democracy items, European Social Survey modules on political values), vignette-based instruments probing trade-offs among democratic principles, and experimental protocols testing messaging on democracy. Also include coding schemes for classifying conceptions in qualitative data. Exclude instruments that measure only institutional indicators without capturing citizen-level conceptions or normative understandings.

instru_desc: Survey instruments, experimental protocols, tracking tools and coding schemes used to measure consumer behavior.
instru_narr: Include questionnaires and scales for attitudes and intentions, purchase diaries, point-of-sale scanner protocols, choice experiment designs, conjoint analysis tools, eye-tracking and clickstream measurement protocols, field/online experimental scripts, and coding manuals for observational shopper studies. Exclude instruments devoted exclusively to firm accounting, manufacturing processes, or non-consumer economic metrics.

instru_desc: Diagnostic protocols, survey instruments, epidemiological models and measurement tools used in COVID-19 research.
instru_narr: Include PCR and antigen testing protocols, serological assay descriptions, standardized COVID-19 symptom checklists, validated survey modules on pandemic behavior and attitudes, contact-tracing system descriptions, mobility-tracking methodologies, statistical and epidemiological modeling tools (SEIR models, R estimation), and clinical-trial protocols for COVID-19 interventions. Exclude laboratory methods unrelated to SARS-CoV-2 and tools intended for non-pandemic infectious disease contexts unless adapted for COVID-19.

instru_desc: Survey questions, coding manuals, and indices used to measure democratic practices, institutions, and attitudes.
instru_narr: Include validated questionnaire modules on political participation and democratic satisfaction, coding schemes and manuals for regime classification (Polity, V-Dem codebooks), electoral data collection protocols, and interview guides for qualitative studies of democratic institutions. Exclude tools developed only for non-political administrative measurement or tools that measure broad governance without reference to democratic criteria.

instru_desc: Validated screening tools, diagnostic interviews, treatment protocols, and assessment batteries for depression research.
instru_narr: Include instruments such as the PHQ-9, Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), CES-D, Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HDRS), SCID diagnostic interview, Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI), psychotherapy manuals, clinical-trial protocols, and standardized rating procedures. Exclude unvalidated mood checklists or single-item measures that do not reliably assess depressive symptoms or diagnoses.

instru_desc: Assessment tools, surveys, analytics methods and protocols used to measure and study digital technology use and its effects.
instru_narr: Include digital-literacy assessment instruments, standardized ICT-use questionnaires, web and app analytics tools and protocols, platform API datasets and scraping methodologies, user-experience testing protocols, and measures for digital inclusion/exclusion. Exclude tools solely for hardware benchmarking or non-human machine performance metrics that do not inform social science questions about digitalization.

instru_desc: Assessment instruments, competency frameworks and measurement tools for digital competence.
instru_narr: Include validated questionnaires, standardized test batteries, competency frameworks (e.g. DigComp, ISTE standards), rubrics for digital task performance, observational protocols, item banks for assessing digital literacy, and manuals documenting administration and scoring. Also include digital learning/training curricula and validated pre/post questionnaires used in interventions. Exclude proprietary instruments with no documentation, technical software tools unrelated to assessment (e.g. server monitoring), or general ICT infrastructure checklists that do not assess human competence.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and tools for researching digitalization and work.
instru_narr: Include surveys and questionnaires for firms and employees on ICT use and digital task content, task-based job analysis instruments, occupational classification crosswalks (to map tasks to automation risk), skill demand taxonomies, employer survey modules, audit tools for workplace digital maturity, and software to analyze job postings or platform work data. Include validated measurement guides and coding manuals. Exclude technical IT deployment manuals and proprietary HR systems without methodological documentation.

instru_desc: Tools and instruments for assessing workplace digitalization and its impacts.
instru_narr: Include workplace assessment checklists, digital maturity models, staff surveys and interview protocols focusing on digital tool adoption and task change, observational protocols for workflow analysis, training evaluation instruments, and guidance documents for implementing digital change. Also include coding schemes for categorizing workplace technologies and task types. Exclude general ICT procurement guides lacking research-oriented measurement detail.

instru_desc: Measurement frameworks and instruments for studying digitization's impact on work and occupations.
instru_narr: Include validated survey modules for ICT and digital task measurement, job analysis tools that classify task content by digital intensity, instruments to measure skill mismatch, software for text-mining job ads to extract digital skill demand, and guidelines for mapping technologies to occupations. Include coding manuals and replication resources. Exclude developer-oriented tools that measure system performance without linking to human work.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools for measuring discrimination, bias and school climate.
instru_narr: Include validated survey instruments for perceived discrimination and school climate, observational protocols for classroom interactions, teacher implicit bias tests (e.g. adapted IATs), coding schemes for disciplinary decisions, measurement tools for tracking and streamlining practices, evaluation frameworks for anti-discrimination programs, and interview/qualitative guides for investigating discriminatory experiences. Include manuals and psychometric documentation. Exclude informal checklists without validation or tools unrelated to school-level discrimination measurement.

instru_desc: Surveys, scales, experimental protocols, audit study designs, coding schemes, and measurement instruments developed to assess discrimination and related constructs.
instru_narr: Include validated questionnaires and scales measuring perceived or experienced discrimination, standardized modules used in social surveys, protocols for field experiments and correspondence/audit studies, coding manuals for discrimination case records, and psychometric evaluations of discrimination measures. Exclude instruments unrelated to social discrimination (e.g., technical discrimination algorithms in signal processing) and generic survey tools lacking discrimination content.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and tools used in education research: standardized tests, assessment batteries, curriculum evaluation tools, survey modules on education, and program evaluation protocols.
instru_narr: Include validated achievement tests, assessment instruments (e.g., reading/math tests), survey modules and questionnaires about schooling and educational attainment, teacher and school evaluation tools, and protocols for implementing and evaluating educational interventions. Exclude general-purpose survey tools without education modules and instruments from unrelated technical domains.

instru_desc: Survey questions, scales, experimental vignettes, and coding schemes developed to measure attitudes toward Islam and related constructs (Islamophobia, social distance, threat perceptions).
instru_narr: Include validated attitude scales and survey modules on Islam/Muslims, feeling thermometer items, social distance scales adapted for Muslim targets, vignettes and experimental protocols assessing bias toward Muslims, and coding manuals for media or discourse analysis about Islam. Exclude measurement tools unrelated to attitudes toward Islam or generic instruments without adaptation to Muslim targets.

instru_desc: Survey modules, scales, vignettes, and experimental protocols designed to measure or influence attitudes toward immigration and migrants.
instru_narr: Include standardized question batteries on immigration attitudes, validated threat and social distance scales adapted for migrants, experimental vignette designs manipulating immigrant characteristics, and coding schemes for media or political discourse about migration. Exclude measurement tools not tailored to migration attitudes or purely administrative tools about migration processes.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments for attitudes toward foreigners: survey questions, xenophobia scales, experimental vignettes, and coding schemes for discourse about foreigners.
instru_narr: Include validated scales and survey modules assessing xenophobia and attitudes toward foreigners, social distance measures, experimental protocols testing bias against foreigners, and tools for content analysis of media or political rhetoric about foreigners. Exclude instruments unrelated to social attitudes or those focusing on diplomatic/legal definitions rather than public perceptions of people.

instru_desc: Questionnaires, survey modules, scales and coding schemes used to measure attitudes to foreigners: social distance scales (e.g., Bogardus items), prejudice/xenophobia indexes, contact measures, and vignette instruments.
instru_narr: Include validated instruments and bespoke survey modules that measure attitudes toward foreigners or immigrants (e.g., Bogardus Social Distance Scale items adapted for immigrants, threat/perceived competition scales, feeling thermometer items, experimental vignettes manipulating immigrant characteristics). Also include coding manuals and question wordings used in major surveys. Exclude measurement tools unrelated to social attitudes (e.g., clinical scales) and instruments that only measure immigrant demographics without attitudinal items.

instru_desc: Questionnaires and measurement tools used to assess gender attitudes: standardized scales (e.g., Ambivalent Sexism Inventory), ISSP/EFA gender modules, question batteries on gender roles, and coding schemes for gender-attitude items.
instru_narr: Include validated instruments and commonly used survey question wordings for measuring gender attitudes (Ambivalent Sexism Inventory, Gender Role Attitudes scales, ISSP Family and Changing Gender Roles module items), guidance on constructing indices, and experimental vignettes manipulating gender cues. Exclude instruments that measure biological sex or gender identity only, or clinical instruments unrelated to social attitudes.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and survey modules for attitudes toward Islam: Islamophobia scales, social distance questionnaires, question wordings on Muslim-related policies, and vignette experiments concerning Muslim characteristics.
instru_narr: Include validated scales and commonly used items for measuring anti-Muslim attitudes (e.g., Islamophobia Scale adaptations), Bogardus-style social distance items tailored to Muslims, policy-question batteries (e.g., mosque, dress codes), and experimental vignettes manipulating religious identity. Also include coding guides and translations of question wordings. Exclude theological assessment tools or instruments measuring Muslim religiosity without items on public attitudes toward Islam.

instru_desc: Survey instruments and administrative tools used to measure employment in Poland: LFS questionnaires, national employment survey modules, coding manuals (ISCO/NACE), and administrative data linkage protocols.
instru_narr: Include full question wordings from labor force and employment surveys used in Poland (Polish LFS, EU-LFS modules), standardized occupation and industry coding schemes (ISCO, NACE), wage imputation procedures, and documentation for linking administrative employment records. Also include questionnaires for employment histories and job quality assessments. Exclude instruments unrelated to employment measurement or those applicable only outside the Polish context without adaptation.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments for work alienation: validated scales (e.g., Seeman's scales, Blauner’s items), questionnaires for autonomy/control, job meaning scales, and coding manuals for constructing alienation indices.
instru_narr: Include established instruments and question batteries measuring work alienation and its subdimensions (e.g., Seeman's alienation constructs, Work Alienation Scale adaptations, items on autonomy and meaningfulness), survey modules from EWCS or company HR surveys, and guidance on index construction and validation. Also include qualitative interview guides focusing on alienation experiences at work. Exclude general wellbeing instruments not tied to work context unless they incorporate workplace-specific items.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and tools used in environmental research: ecological assessment protocols, environmental attitude scales, sensors and monitoring devices, GIS tools, and survey modules (e.g., ISSP/ESS environment modules).
instru_narr: Include validated attitude scales (e.g., NEP), standardized monitoring protocols, sensor specifications and calibration procedures, GIS/remote sensing workflows, and survey modules designed to capture environmental attitudes, behaviours and perceptions. Exclude generic measurement tools that are not applied to environmental measurement (e.g., general psychometric scales with no environmental items) unless adapted for environmental research.

instru_desc: Validated instruments and survey modules for measuring environmental attitudes: NEP scale, Environmental Concern scales, ISSP/ESS environment modules, and experimental vignettes for attitude measurement.
instru_narr: Include multi-item scales (e.g., New Ecological Paradigm), standard survey modules (ISSP Environment, ESS environment-related items), validated short-form scales, question batteries with phrasing and response options, and measurement guides. Also include tools for scale validation (factor analysis scripts, reliability coefficients). Exclude generic attitude instruments that do not include environmental content.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and pedagogical tools used in research on Erziehung: parenting questionnaires, HOME inventory, standardized child development tests, teacher-report scales, and curriculum/intervention materials.
instru_narr: Include validated parenting and family functioning questionnaires (e.g., Parenting Styles and Dimensions Questionnaire), observational protocols, early childhood assessment tools, teacher rating instruments, and intervention manuals for parenting or educational programs. Include German-language instruments or translations and documentation of reliability/validity. Exclude tools that are not designed to measure upbringing, parenting or educational processes.

instru_desc: Evaluation instruments and tools for social work: outcome measurement scales, case management systems, logic models, standardized assessment tools (e.g., HoNOS, CORE-OM where applicable), and guidelines for programme evaluation in social work.
instru_narr: Include validated outcome scales used in social care, structured assessment tools, protocols for routine outcome monitoring, implementation fidelity checklists, cost-effectiveness templates, and evaluation toolkits tailored to social work practice (including German-language toolkits). Also include qualitative evaluation guides and mixed-methods instruments commonly used in social work evaluations. Exclude general evaluation tools that are not adapted to social work contexts unless documented as applied successfully in social work settings.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and survey modules used to assess external political efficacy: validated scale items, survey batteries from major studies (ANES, ESS, ISSP), and analytic tools for constructing efficacy indices.
instru_narr: Include standard question wordings and response formats for external efficacy items, validated multi-item scales where available, harmonization guides for cross-national comparison, and codebooks/scripts for scale construction and reliability testing. Exclude measurement tools that only address internal efficacy or general civic attitudes without items on institutional responsiveness.

instru_desc: Survey modules, time‑use diaries, life‑history calendars, administrative linkage protocols, employer questionnaires, and standard scales measuring work–family conflict and reconciliation policies.
instru_narr: Include instruments used to collect or measure work–family data: household roster modules, employment histories, occupational coding schemes (e.g., ISCO), standardized time‑use diaries, validated scales for work–family conflict/work‑life balance (e.g., Netemeyer work–family conflict items), parental leave and childcare modules, life history calendars capturing career and family events, employer survey instruments on flexible work, and protocols for linking administrative employment/benefit records to family registers. Exclude instruments focused only on clinical assessment or unrelated domains.

instru_desc: Career history modules, employer HR surveys, life‑history calendars, promotion and salary coding schemes, qualitative interview guides on career and family balancing.
instru_narr: Include instruments for capturing career trajectories and family timing: structured career history questionnaires, administrative payroll and HR data extraction tools, life course calendars mapping births and job changes, occupational coding (ISCO), pay scale coding, standardized measures of career progression and ambition, and semi‑structured interview guides exploring career decisions after family events. Exclude instruments not designed to record temporal links between family and career.

instru_desc: Standardized attitude batteries (e.g., ESS gender items), time‑use diary instruments, household task inventories, qualitative interview guides on gender and family, and coding schemes for task allocation.
instru_narr: Include measurement instruments used to study changing gender roles: survey modules on gender role attitudes (items from ESS, WVS, Eurobarometer), validated scales for egalitarianism, 24‑hour or activity‑based time‑use diaries, household chore checklists, life history interviews capturing shifts in role expectations, observational protocols for family interaction, and methods for coding and quantifying task division. Exclude tools not applicable to measuring gendered behaviour or attitudes in family contexts.

instru_desc: Household rosters, family history calendars, vital record linkage protocols, time‑use instruments, parenting questionnaires, kinship matrix coding schemes, and qualitative interview guides on family life.
instru_narr: Include instruments for collecting family data: standard household roster modules, life‑history and event history calendars capturing marriages and births, protocols for linking administrative vital records to survey data, 24‑hour and episode‑based time‑use diaries, parenting and caregiving scales, intergenerational transfer modules, and semi‑structured interview guides on family relationships. Include classification schemes for household types and kinship coding. Exclude instruments that do not support constructing family or household indicators.

instru_desc: Gender attitude batteries, sex‑disaggregated time‑use diaries, household chore inventories, parental leave registries by sex, interview guides on gendered family roles, and coding schemes for gendered task allocation.
instru_narr: Include instruments designed to capture gendered dimensions of family life: validated gender‑attitude items (ESS/WVS), 24‑hour and activity‑based time‑use instruments with respondent sex, modules on distribution of household tasks, administrative registries recording parental leave by gender, qualitative interview protocols probing gendered decision making and care practices, and analytical tools for coding and quantifying gendered divisions of labour. Exclude measurement tools that do not distinguish gender or cannot be applied to family contexts.

instru_desc: Questionnaire modules, coding manuals and classification schemes used to collect and code employment form data: employment status modules, contract-type questions, working hours modules, ILO and EU-LFS question sets, labor market coding manuals and job exposure matrices for precariousness.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments: standard labor force survey question batteries (ILO/EU-LFS style), national microcensus employment modules, panel survey employment modules (SOEP/GSOEP employment history), employer-employee survey modules on contract characteristics, and coding schemes for temporary vs. permanent contracts. Include documentation on harmonization protocols and translation notes. Exclude instruments that only measure firm-level characteristics unrelated to individual contract or that lack items on contract/arrangement type.

instru_desc: Validated scales and survey modules in German or with German translations used to measure leadership and trust: Mayer & Davis trust scales, McAllister affective/cognitive trust scale, LMX-7, scales for trust in management and leader integrity, and leadership questionnaires (e.g., MLQ) that include trust-related subscales.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments: instruments that explicitly assess trust in leaders or trust-relevant leader behaviors (Mayer & Davis, McAllister, LMX measures), German-language adaptations and manuals, leadership questionnaires (MLQ, authentic leadership scales) when linked to trust outcomes, and coding documentation for aggregated trust measures. Exclude instruments that measure only general social trust without leader referent or tools that assess unrelated concepts (e.g., tourist guiding surveys).

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and assessment tools for leadership: Multifactor Leadership Questionnaire (MLQ), Leader–Member Exchange (LMX) scales, Leadership Practices Inventory (LPI), 360-degree feedback instruments, situational judgment tests and leadership competency frameworks, including German translations/adaptations.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments: validated leadership questionnaires (MLQ, LPI, LMX-7), 360-degree feedback protocols, leadership development program evaluation tools, coding manuals and translation/adaptation documentation. Include psychometric properties and administration guidelines. Exclude instruments that do not measure leadership constructs or that are intended for unrelated tasks (e.g., tourist guide evaluations).

instru_desc: Validated questionnaires and modules for measuring gender roles and attitudes: Attitudes Toward Women Scale (AWS), Bem Sex Role Inventory (BSRI), Gender Role Ideology scales, ISSP/ESS/WVS gender-role modules and coding guides.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments: survey modules and psychometric scales that assess gender-role beliefs and identities, their German-language adaptations, and codebooks with item wording and coding schemes. Include documentation on scoring, reliability and translations. Exclude instruments unrelated to gender norms (e.g., generic role-identity tools without gender focus).

instru_desc: Survey modules, questionnaires and coding guides for measuring gender and related constructs: two-step gender identity items, Gender Identity/Gender Minority measures, gender norms modules (ESS, ISSP items), and documentation for coding sex/gender in administrative data.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments: validated items and best-practice question wording (two-step method: sex assigned at birth + current gender), scales measuring gender norms and expression, and coding manuals addressing non-binary and transgender categories. Include guidelines on ethical collection of gender data and translation notes for different languages. Exclude instruments that conflate sex and gender without clear items or lack documentation on response options and coding.

instru_desc: Validated scales, survey modules, interview guides and coding schemes used to measure gender attitudes, roles, identities and related constructs.
instru_narr: Include: instruments such as Bem Sex Role Inventory, Gender Role Attitudes scales, gender ideology items, interview/observation guides for gender studies, coding schemes for qualitative gender analysis, and standardized modules (e.g., ISSP/ESS gender modules). Exclude: clinical diagnostic tools unrelated to social gender (e.g., endocrine assays), or tools focused solely on biological sex measurement without social/gender components.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and manuals for assessing general self‑efficacy, their translations, scoring rules and validation studies.
instru_narr: Include: General Self‑Efficacy Scale (Schwarzer & Jerusalem) and its validated language versions, psychometric papers, item lists, scoring instructions, administration guidelines, and short/long form variants. Exclude: instruments that measure only domain‑specific self‑efficacy (e.g., Academic Self‑Efficacy Scale) unless they include a general self‑efficacy component.

instru_desc: Survey modules, questionnaires and analytic tools designed or commonly used to study generational cohorts, and methods for cohort assignment and age‑period‑cohort analysis.
instru_narr: Include: questionnaires with items on values, technology use, work preferences tailored to Millennials, codebooks that flag generational cohorts, and statistical tools/methods for cohort comparison (APC models). Exclude: tools unrelated to cohort identification or analyses that do not support cohort stratification.

instru_desc: German instruments and translations for measuring general self‑efficacy, manuals, item lists and validation studies (e.g., Suche for 'Allgemeine Selbstwirksamkeitserwartung').
instru_narr: Include: German version of the General Self‑Efficacy Scale (Schwarzer & Jerusalem), translation/adaptation documentation, scoring instructions, normative data for German populations, and psychometric studies. Exclude: instruments that only measure domain‑specific Selbstwirksamkeit and lack a general component.

instru_desc: Validated scales, survey questions, interview guides and coding manuals used to measure gender roles, role attitudes and gendered behaviour.
instru_narr: Include: instruments like the Bem Sex Role Inventory, Attitudes Toward Women Scale, Gender Role Attitudes items found in ISSP/ESS, time‑use survey instruments, qualitative interview guides on gender socialization, and coding schemes for role content analysis. Exclude: biological measurement tools and instruments not addressing social role constructs.

instru_desc: Validated scales and survey modules used to assess gender roles, plus coding schemes and questionnaires relevant to role attitudes and behaviors.
instru_narr: Include instruments such as the Bem Sex Role Inventory (BSRI), Attitudes Toward Women Scale, Gender Role Attitudes items in ISSP/ESS, role conflict/strain scales, time-use instruments that allow computing division of labor, and translations/adaptations of these tools in German. Also include coding guides and questionnaire modules used in large surveys to capture gender-role data. Exclude clinical instruments unrelated to social role measurement and generic organizational job-role tools that do not address gender.

instru_desc: Survey modules, scales and qualitative protocols used to measure gender-role attitudes and stereotypes, and comparative coding schemes for cross-cultural research.
instru_narr: Include instruments like ISSP and ESS gender/family modules, Bem Sex Role Inventory and its adaptations, Attitudes Toward Women Scale, stereotype endorsement items, standardized time-use diaries, and interview guides for qualitative studies of gender norms. Exclude instruments that do not pertain to gender norms or role expectations.

instru_desc: Validated health measurement instruments and tools: health surveys, clinical assessment instruments, questionnaires, and coding systems used in health research.
instru_narr: Include instruments such as SF-36/SF-12, EQ-5D, WHO health surveys, GHQ, standardized clinical assessment protocols, laboratory assay methods, and coding systems like ICD and ATC. Also include population health surveillance tools and measurement guides. Exclude instruments unrelated to health measurement (e.g. purely administrative business tools).

instru_desc: Psychometric instruments and clinical tools for assessing mental health: screening questionnaires, diagnostic interviews, standardized clinical scales and service-use measurement instruments.
instru_narr: Include commonly used validated instruments such as PHQ-9, GAD-7, GHQ-12, BDI, HADS, WHO-5, MINI, SCID, and service-use questionnaires and PROMs for mental health. Also include coding schemes for psychiatric diagnoses (ICD-10/DSM) and assessment protocols used in clinical and epidemiological studies. Exclude tools not validated for mental health assessment or instruments intended solely for neurological testing without psychiatric relevance.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools for assessing patient health and experience: clinical outcome measures, PROMs, satisfaction surveys, clinical assessment protocols and registries.
instru_narr: Include tools such as PROMIS, EQ-5D, SF-36, disease-specific outcome scales, patient satisfaction instruments (e.g. HCAHPS where applicable), clinical case report forms, standardized follow-up protocols, and registries used to monitor patient outcomes. Exclude instruments not intended for patient assessment or administrative tools unrelated to patient health.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools used for assessing and implementing workplace health programs, organizational risk assessments, and OSH management systems.
instru_narr: Include validated questionnaires and checklists for workplace health promotion and occupational safety (e.g., workplace health climate scales, organizational-level psychosocial risk assessment tools), implementation toolkits for enterprises, intervention manuals, company-level audit instruments, and employer survey instruments. Exclude clinical diagnostic instruments used only in medical settings, instruments solely measuring general population health unrelated to workplace, or tools designed exclusively for patient care.

instru_desc: Assessment instruments and implementation tools for measuring and improving health in workplace settings.
instru_narr: Include validated employee health questionnaires (e.g., job-content questionnaires, effort–reward imbalance scales, workplace stress inventories), ergonomic assessment tools, workplace risk assessment protocols, intervention toolkits used in companies, and monitoring instruments for occupational exposures. Exclude instruments intended only for clinical diagnosis outside occupational assessment or tools not applicable to workplace settings.

instru_desc: Survey instruments, clinical measures, and occupational assessment tools used to measure employee health and work-related exposures.
instru_narr: Include validated health questionnaires for working populations (e.g., GHQ, SF-12/36, WHO-5), scales for work stress and psychosocial risks, instruments for measuring absenteeism/presenteeism, occupational exposure measurement tools, and protocols for workplace health examinations. Exclude instruments intended for general population screening when not validated for employed subgroups, or tools unrelated to occupational health assessment.

instru_desc: Questionnaires and measurement tools for assessing health complaints and symptom burden.
instru_narr: Include validated symptom checklists and inventories (e.g., SCL-90 somatisation items, somatic symptom scales, standardized pain questionnaires), daily symptom diaries, sleep disturbance instruments, and occupational symptom assessment tools. Also include protocols for clinical evaluation of symptom complaints in occupational health. Exclude purely laboratory instruments that do not measure subjective complaints.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and tools for assessing violence exposure, perpetration, and response, and for implementing prevention/intervention programs.
instru_narr: Include validated survey instruments and screening tools (e.g., Conflict Tactics Scale, WHO Violence Against Women instrument, juvenile delinquency/violence scales), incident reporting protocols, risk assessment tools, observational coding schemes for violent events, and program manuals for prevention/intervention (e.g., bystander training, domestic violence interventions). Exclude forensic lab methods unrelated to social measurement, instruments only for animal behavior, or tools that do not capture human-directed violence.

instru_desc: Validated instruments and screening tools used to assess violence involving youth, prevention program measures, and standardized questionnaires for child/adolescent violence.
instru_narr: Include instruments such as the Juvenile Victimization Questionnaire (JVQ), Conflict Tactics Scales (CTS) adapted for adolescents, Olweus Bullying Questionnaire, Cyberbullying scales, Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ) for retrospective adolescent reports, school-based victimization modules, and standardized screening tools used by child protection services. Also include evaluation tools for youth violence prevention programs. Exclude adult-only violence instruments without youth validation and generic crime-record extraction protocols that lack measures specific to children or adolescents.

instru_desc: Standard instruments and survey items used to assess life satisfaction and facilitate cross-national comparability.
instru_narr: Include validated instruments such as the Cantril ladder, the Satisfaction With Life Scale (SWLS), OECD's single life satisfaction item, and standardized questionnaire modules from World Values Survey, ESS, Gallup, and ISSP used for global comparability. Also include translation and harmonization protocols, anchoring vignettes and methods/tools for testing measurement invariance across cultures. Exclude ad hoc or unvalidated single items without comparability information and instruments intended only for clinical diagnostic use unrelated to life evaluation.

instru_desc: Validated instruments and measurement tools commonly used in population health research and public health surveillance.
instru_narr: Include instruments such as SF-36/SF-12 (health-related quality of life), EQ-5D, PHQ-9, GAD-7, GHQ-12, AUDIT, standardized physical activity and dietary questionnaires, clinical measurement protocols for blood pressure/BMI, and survey modules from WHO STEPS, DHS, and national health interview surveys. Also include coding schemes for ICD diagnoses in administrative data and tools for health inequality measurement. Exclude highly specialized laboratory assay kits or clinical devices not used in population-level measurement.

instru_desc: Survey modules, scales and measurement tools used to assess telework practices, remote work outcomes, and home-office ergonomics.
instru_narr: Include validated survey items and modules for measuring telework frequency and intensity, remote-work environment checklists, work–family conflict scales (e.g., Carlson et al. work–family conflict scale), remote-work productivity/self-efficacy measures, time-use diary instruments capturing work location, and ergonomic self-assessment checklists for home offices. Also include employer policy templates and evaluation tools for remote work programs. Exclude generic IT configuration guides or product-specific setup manuals unrelated to research measurement.

instru_desc: Standard instruments, questionnaires and coding schemes used in migration research, and tools for measuring integration and legal status.
instru_narr: Include survey modules and question batteries for migration (e.g., migrant background question sets used in EU surveys), language proficiency assessments, integration scales (social, economic, civic integration indices), legal-status coding schemes, and tools for harmonizing migration variables across datasets (e.g., harmonization guides for country of birth, citizenship, and year of arrival). Also include translations/translation protocols for migrant surveys and instruments for measuring xenophobia or attitudes toward immigrants. Exclude administrative IT systems unrelated to research use and instruments designed solely for immigration officers' operational use without research documentation.

instru_desc: Questionnaires, survey modules, scales, measurement protocols, and software/tools used to collect or analyze inequality-related data and to compute distributional statistics and decomposition methods.
instru_narr: Include survey instruments that capture income, consumption, employment, education, health, and household characteristics; coding manuals; tools for measuring inequality (Gini calculators, decomposition routines, microsimulation models); and software packages and reproducible code for inequality analysis. Exclude instruments unrelated to distributional measurement (e.g., clinical instruments without socioeconomic variables) and tools that only visualize non-distributional data.

instru_desc: Survey instruments, experimental protocols, coding schemes, annotation guidelines, and software/tools for measuring and analyzing trust in information and credibility assessments.
instru_narr: Include questionnaires and validated scales for media or source trust, experimental designs for credibility interventions, coding manuals for annotating trustworthiness of content, fact-checking frameworks, and analytical tools for sentiment/credibility detection. Exclude technical tools that only perform linguistic processing without relevance to trust measurement, unless paired with trust annotation protocols.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools for studying information policy and politics: policy coding schemes, legal databases, FOI request templates, content censorship monitors, and analytical tools for mapping political information flows.
instru_narr: Include coding manuals and typologies for classifying information policies, structured templates for collecting FOI data, tools for monitoring and geolocating censorship or takedown events, and software for network analysis of political information dissemination. Exclude purely engineering tools for information systems administration that do not support political/policy research.

instru_desc: Survey instruments, measurement protocols, digital skills tests, usage diaries, and tools for measuring ICT infrastructure and digital engagement.
instru_narr: Include standardized questionnaires for ICT access and use (e.g., household ICT modules), validated digital literacy assessments, log collection protocols, website/app analytics frameworks for research, and geospatial tools for mapping connectivity. Exclude developer tools and software components intended solely for building ICT systems without measurement or research application.

instru_desc: Survey questions, modules, validated scales, and experimental protocols used to measure political interest and related constructs (attention, civic engagement).
instru_narr: Include standard questionnaire items and modules from election studies and international surveys that capture political interest, interview protocols, diary instruments for media attention, and experimental designs testing causal effects on interest. Exclude administrative tools or institutional records that do not directly measure individual political interest.

instru_desc: Questionnaires, scales and measurement tools that assess interest in leadership or aspiration to lead (e.g., leadership aspiration items, leadership motivation scales), as well as structured interview protocols and vignette measures that elicit willingness to assume leadership.
instru_narr: Include validated instruments or bespoke survey items that directly measure interest in leadership, promotion intent, or leadership career goals. Include experimental choice tasks and vignettes designed to elicit leadership preference. Exclude tools that measure general leadership ability, leader behavior, or organizational leadership climate when they do not measure individual interest or aspiration to lead.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and tools used to assess work motivation: standardized questionnaires (e.g., WEIMS, UWES), situational judgment tests, diaries measuring daily motivation, intervention toolkits, and observational coding schemes for motivational behavior at work.
instru_narr: Include validated questionnaires and measurement protocols that target motivational constructs in occupational settings, daily experience-sampling tools for motivation at work, and experimental paradigms designed to manipulate or assess motivation. Exclude instruments developed for school or clinical contexts unless explicitly adapted and validated for workplace use.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments for job satisfaction such as the Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire (MSQ), Job Descriptive Index (JDI), single-item global satisfaction measures, and survey modules used in employee studies.
instru_narr: Include validated scales and commonly used survey items that measure overall and facet job satisfaction, along with administration guidelines and scoring procedures. Exclude instruments unrelated to job satisfaction (e.g., general life satisfaction scales) unless tied explicitly to the job domain.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools for researching adolescents: youth questionnaires, standardized screening instruments (SDQ, CES-DC), school survey instruments, developmental assessment tools, and protocols for interviewing minors (parental consent procedures).
instru_narr: Include age-appropriate validated instruments and survey modules tailored to adolescents, tools for assessing mental and physical health, and instruments for educational and social behavior research. Exclude adult-focused instruments unless validated for adolescent populations.

instru_desc: Measurement tools used with children and adolescents: Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL), Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), pediatric quality-of-life scales, developmental assessment batteries, school achievement tests, and consent/assent protocols.
instru_narr: Include validated, age-appropriate instruments and assessment protocols for children and adolescents, as well as survey modules designed for caregivers or schools. Exclude instruments validated only for adults or those unsuitable for minors without documented adaptation and validation.

instru_desc: Measurement and analytic instruments for climate science and social research on climate: meteorological sensors, remote sensing platforms, climate models, climate indices, survey instruments for climate attitudes, vulnerability/adaptation assessment tools.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments include weather stations, satellite sensors, ocean buoys, global/regional climate models (GCMs/RCMs), reanalysis products, standard climate indices (e.g., SPI, SPEI, Köppen classification), and validated survey questionnaires on climate attitudes and risk perception. Exclude general-purpose measurement tools with no explicit application to climate topics.

instru_desc: Tools for studying climate change: attribution methods, earth system and integrated assessment models, emission calculators, vulnerability/resilience assessment frameworks, survey instruments measuring climate change perceptions and behavior, and decision-support tools for mitigation/adaptation.
instru_narr: Include climate models (GCMs/ESMs), statistical attribution techniques, IAMs, carbon footprint calculators, adaptation planning tools (e.g., climate risk assessments), and validated questionnaires on climate change beliefs and actions. Exclude tools with no explicit application to climate change research.

instru_desc: Tools and instruments for cultural research: standardized survey modules on culture and identity, cultural participation questionnaires, ethnographic interview guides, coding schemes for qualitative cultural data, cultural policy evaluation frameworks, and cultural heritage inventories.
instru_narr: Include validated survey instruments measuring cultural engagement and values, structured interview guides for ethnography, content analysis coding schemes for cultural texts, and methodological toolkits for evaluating cultural policy and heritage. Exclude biomedical laboratory tools or instruments unrelated to humanities/social scientific study of culture.

instru_desc: Instruments for researching workplace learning: training evaluation tools, workplace learning questionnaires, competency assessments, observational protocols for workplace learning, employer survey modules, and tools for measuring informal learning and knowledge transfer.
instru_narr: Include standardized instruments for assessing training participation and outcomes, validated competency tests, interview guides and observation checklists for workplace learning episodes, and employer questionnaires on training provision. Exclude instruments designed solely for classroom education or for automated/machine learning evaluation.

instru_desc: Instruments for measuring left-right orientation: survey questions for ideological self-placement, battery of policy attitude items for scale construction, psychometric tools for dimensionality analysis, party position coding schemes, and Q-methodology protocols for ideological mapping.
instru_narr: Include standard left-right self-placement items, validated issue batteries to derive ideological scales, coding manuals for placing parties/manifestos on left-right spectra, and statistical tools (factor analysis, IRT) used to validate left-right measures. Exclude instruments not related to political ideology measurement.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and tools for media research: survey questionnaires, coding schemes for content analysis, media diaries, web-scraping and social media collection tools, platform APIs, and validated scales measuring media-related constructs.
instru_narr: Relevant instruments include validated survey items and scales for media exposure and media literacy, content analysis codebooks and intercoder reliability protocols, media diaries and experience sampling instruments, tools and scripts for collecting social media data (APIs, crawlers), sentiment and topic analysis pipelines, and methodological protocols for experimental media research. Include documentation, manuals, and codebooks that enable replication. Exclude instruments solely for biological media cultivation, manufacturing quality control, or hardware diagnostics unrelated to communication research.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools to assess characteristics of work: job-content questionnaires, psychosocial risk scales, ergonomics checklists, workplace observation protocols, and occupational classification tools.
instru_narr: Include validated instruments such as the Job Content Questionnaire (JCQ), Effort-Reward Imbalance (ERI) scales, Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaire (COPSOQ), O*NET or ISCO-based task inventories, workplace hazard assessment checklists, time-use diaries, and structured job-analysis protocols. Also include measurement manuals, codebooks, and interviewer guides for assessing job attributes. Exclude tools unrelated to measuring job characteristics (e.g., general HR software without assessment modules) or instruments focused only on organizational performance without job-level measurement.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools for migration research: survey modules and questionnaires capturing migration histories, migration registers, tracking protocols, qualitative interview guides, and coding schemes for legal statuses and reasons for migration.
instru_narr: Include standardized survey modules (e.g., migration history modules), census questions templates on place of birth and previous residence, administrative register schemas, interview guides for migrant experiences, protocols for longitudinal tracking and sampling of mobile populations, and classification tools for legal statuses and migrant typologies. Also include GIS and mobility-tracking tools used in migration studies. Exclude laboratory tools for biological migration or instruments not designed to measure human mobility and migration processes.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools for employee research: staff survey questionnaires, HR information systems, performance appraisal instruments, employee engagement scales, exit interview protocols, and staff audit tools.
instru_narr: Include validated employee-focused instruments such as job satisfaction scales, engagement and commitment questionnaires, 360-degree feedback tools, performance appraisal forms, HR administrative data schemas, staff climate and culture surveys, and interview guides used in employee studies. Also include codebooks and manuals for employee datasets. Exclude general business software unrelated to measuring or researching employees and tools intended only for volunteer or collaborator tracking not tied to employment.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools for measuring mobility: travel survey questionnaires, GPS/smartphone logging apps, travel diary protocols, transport modeling software, accessibility calculators, and indicators for social mobility analysis.
instru_narr: Include standardized travel diary instruments, GPS and smartphone data collection tools, public transport smartcard data processing tools, origin-destination matrix construction protocols, transport demand and traffic simulation models, GIS tools for accessibility analysis, and survey modules for social mobility (e.g., parental occupation/education modules). Also include manuals, coding schemes, and data processing scripts specific to mobility research. Exclude laboratory instruments measuring molecular mobility or tools unrelated to human or social mobility measurement.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and protocols for assessing employee motivation and workplace engagement (questionnaires, interview guides, observational checklists).
instru_narr: Include validated instruments and tools used in organizational contexts such as the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES), Job Diagnostic Survey (JDS), Minnesota Satisfaction Questionnaire (MSQ), Work Extrinsic and Intrinsic Motivation Scale (WEIMS), organizational climate instruments, structured interview protocols for motivation, and workplace observation schemes. Include descriptions of administration, translation/validation for German contexts, and scoring. Exclude ad-hoc or single-item measures without validation unless clearly described as exploratory tools.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools for measuring motivation in learning: questionnaires, observational protocols, learning analytics methods, and intervention materials.
instru_narr: Include validated scales such as the Academic Motivation Scale (AMS), Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire (MSLQ), Goal Orientation Scales, self-regulated learning instruments, situational interest measures, and coding schemes for classroom motivation. Also include tools for measuring online engagement (clickstream, LMS logs), and instructional materials used in motivation interventions. Exclude instruments that do not measure motivational constructs or that are exclusively for non-learning applications.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and protocols for assessing interest and motivation: interest inventories, situational interest scales, curiosity measures, and complementary observational/analytics tools.
instru_narr: Include validated instruments such as the Situational Interest Scale, Personal Interest Questionnaires, Domain-specific interest inventories, Curiosity scales, and instruments that jointly measure motivation and interest (components of AMS, MSLQ subscales). Also include observational coding schemes and digital measures (e.g., attention/engagement trackers) used to operationalize interest. Exclude tools that measure only consumer preferences or market interest without psychological constructs.

instru_desc: Measurement instruments and tools for assessing media use: questionnaires, time-use diaries, passive digital tracking tools, and coding schemes for content and engagement.
instru_narr: Include validated media use questionnaires, standardized time-use diaries, app and browser logging tools, APIs and analytics methods for social media/platform data collection, and coding manuals for content classification and engagement metrics. Include protocols for ethical data collection and anonymization. Exclude purely network-management tools or content-production software that do not measure user consumption.

instru_desc: Instruments and tools for studying online sport: fitness tracking devices, app/platform analytics, e-sports stat trackers, questionnaires on online exercise behavior, and intervention materials for virtual training.
instru_narr: Include wearable sensors and their data processing protocols, app analytics dashboards, APIs for platform data extraction, validated questionnaires on digital exercise behavior and adherence, performance tracking tools used in e-sports, and manuals for online coaching interventions. Also include methods for measuring user engagement in livestreams. Exclude measurement tools designed solely for in-person sport that have no online adaptation or data export capability.

instru_desc: Questionnaires, standardized tests and program manuals used to assess vocational interests, career decision-making, and guidance interventions.
instru_narr: Include validated instruments and tools such as Self-Directed Search, Holland (RIASEC) inventories, Career Adapt-Abilities Scale, Career Decision-Making Self-Efficacy scales, vocational interest inventories, school/counseling program manuals, assessment batteries used in career guidance, and measurement protocols for tracking transitions. Include translation/adaptation documentation and scoring guides. Exclude instruments focused on unrelated constructs (spatial orientation or political orientation) and employer-only HR tools that do not assess individual vocational orientation.

instru_desc: Standardized personality questionnaires, short-form scales, manuals, scoring keys and validation studies.
instru_narr: Include validated instruments such as NEO-PI-R/3, BFI/10/44, TIPI, IPIP scales, Eysenck inventories, personality disorder instruments, instrument manuals, translation/adaptation documentation, scoring algorithms and psychometric validation reports. Also include computerized assessment tools and coding schemes for personality data. Exclude ad hoc or single-item measures without validation and instruments solely measuring unrelated constructs (e.g., charisma as marketing term).

instru_desc: Survey modules, validated scales and measurement tools used to assess political participation and civic engagement.
instru_narr: Include standardized questionnaire modules from major surveys (ESS, CSES, ANES, ISSP) measuring participation, indexes and scoring rules, experimental mobilization protocols, coding schemes for protest/event participation, and measurement guides for online political behavior. Include translation notes and administration protocols. Exclude tools that do not measure political activity or that are purely administrative (e.g., voter registration lists) without individual-level participation measures.

instru_desc: Question items, scales and measurement protocols for assessing political efficacy and related constructs.
instru_narr: Include validated efficacy items and scales used in ESS, ANES, CSES and other surveys, scale construction guides, psychometric validation studies, question-wording variants and translation notes, and experimental instruments manipulating perceived efficacy. Exclude instruments measuring non-political efficacy (e.g., health self-efficacy) unless adapted and validated for political contexts.

instru_desc: Survey instruments, questionnaires, coding manuals and methodological toolkits for conducting political surveys.
instru_narr: Include full questionnaires and modules used in major political surveys (ESS, ANES, CSES, Eurobarometer), interviewer instructions, translation/adaptation files, sampling designs, weighting guides, question batteries for measuring ideology, turnout and party ID, and tools for questionnaire programming and fieldwork. Exclude non-survey tools (e.g., purely administrative election returns) and instruments not applicable to political survey research.

instru_desc: Survey instruments, questionnaires, coding manuals and measurement tools designed to capture political constructs: election study questionnaires, public opinion modules, manifestos coding schemes, scales for political trust, efficacy, ideology, and tools for political discourse/content analysis.
